title: Leaf count is monotone along subprotocol paths
statement: Let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols over the same input types, and suppose there is a subprotocol path from $s$ to $p$, witnessing that $s$ occurs as a rooted subtree of $p$. Then $s$ has at most as many leaves as $p$; that is, the number of leaves of $s$ is less than or equal to the number of leaves of $p$.
hypotheses_covered: a subprotocol path from s to p exists, witnessing that s is a rooted subtree of p
replaced:
If \texttt{hsp} is a \texttt{SubprotocolPath} from $s$ to $p$, then
$s.\mathrm{numLeaves} \le p.\mathrm{numLeaves}$.  A subtree cannot have more leaves than
its parent.
